attribution.note: Marcus's own commentary in his Substack post, interpreting a CNBC poll in his own words.

semantics.note: Accurately states his inference from the reported 79% figure to rejecting the 'ignoring AI' narrative. It is firm and unhedged. The CNBC survey qualifier is kept.

contract.note: Marcus gave no population or threshold. Reading the claim as general engagement, with trial counting and no majority threshold, is an ordinary plain reading. Separating his personal-trial premise from company use is fair to his actual words.

evidence.note: CNBC's own report, Oct 8-21 2024, from a sample of its tech-executive council. Per the item, the 79% refers to company use of Copilot, not respondents personally trying it. That undercuts Marcus's description of the premise.
Nationally representative US survey: 39% of adults 18-64 used generative AI. Measured in August 2024, outside the October target month, so context only.

Morning Consult/CCIA survey of US adults, October 2024: 44% had used AI services. That shows substantial public engagement in the target month, without imposing a majority threshold. Published Nov 2025, before the cutoff.

reviews.rationale: The broad point holds on the plain reading: in October 2024, 44% of US adults had used AI (e3), which is substantial engagement, not widespread disregard. The cited premise does not hold: CNBC's report says the 79% figure measures company Copilot use, not personal trial (e1), and the sample is a narrow executive council. So the conclusion stands, but the evidence offered for it was misdescribed.
